answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a climbing bond terrace: each new identity must lock a growing collateral slice and publish a unique work receipt that five non-kin established peers countersign. Those receipts are the timber of reputation—slow to harvest, easy to burn if a clone is proven. Farms cannot cheaply mint armies because every extra identity multiplies unrecoverable stake. Only accounts that reach the zenith of independently attested history keep emission and vote weight.
